analysis.title: Novartis (NOVN.S): MNM 2026 - mid-term guidance suggests upside in 2031, MSD growth beyond 2030 reiterated but will likely take time before cons. reflects this
key_insights: Novartis introduced 2026-31 revenue CAGR guidance of 5% at constant exchange rates (GSe 5% vs. consensus 4.3%). GS says this implies upside risk of about 3% to consensus 2031 sales, all else equal.

The stock closed down about 3% after the event, against the SXDP sector index down 1.8%. GS reads this as investors wanting more proof of growth through the end-of-decade patent expirations before adding the upside to estimates. GS also calls the reaction somewhat harsh given the limited new information.

Management reiterated mid-single-digit (MSD) growth beyond 2030. It sees a $20bn gap between 2035 consensus (about $64bn) and the 2035 sales implied by guidance (about $85bn). At least half of the gap could be closed by on-market or near-market assets.

GS stays Sell. MSD growth beyond 2030 looks challenging without more late-stage M&A or above-average clinical success. Patent expirations for Entresto, Cosentyx, Kesimpta and Kisqali could produce a period of growth below 5% into 2031/32.

GS does not include Phase 1 assets in its sales forecasts, so it sees risk to the long-term outlook. At about 15x 2028 P/E, a roughly 15% premium to the sector, GS argues the growth is at least partly in the multiple.

Strategy and capital allocation are unchanged. Business development is expected to focus on deals below $2bn, with M&A/BD around $3-4bn a year and about 50% of revenues from external sources. GS sees buybacks continuing as part of shareholder returns through at least 2031.

Management targets core operating margin of 40% or more by 2029 and sustained after. The drivers are sales growth and SG&A leverage, with R&D held as a stable percentage of sales. Headwinds are Entresto genericisation, Xolair profit-sharing and IRA pricing.

Rhapsido (remibrutinib) is a key growth driver with $8bn peak sales across indications with Phase 3 data. Management sees about $1bn peak in HS. GS models $9.5bn at 85% average probability of success.

Pipeline peak-sales estimates from GS: abelacimab $2.2bn (60% probability of success), pacibekitug $2bn (low probability of success after the negative ZEUS read-through) and ianalumab $5bn. GS does not model GHZ339 because its mechanism was only disclosed at the event.

Novartis flagged 8 potentially positive submission-enabling readouts across 6 assets in 2027. Key ones are abelacimab in atrial fibrillation stroke prevention (event driven, interim passed) and ianalumab in lupus nephritis, systemic lupus and systemic sclerosis. A Q1'27 FDA meeting could allow early filing of votoplam in Huntington's.

Kesimpta peak-sales guidance was upgraded to $8bn, with remibrutinib positioned as a $4bn+ relapsing MS opportunity. Novartis still assumes 2031 composition-of-matter loss of exclusivity for Kesimpta.

Kisqali $10bn peak sales is seen as achievable. Management expects US sales to decline in 2028 with IRA implementation while volumes grow, in line with the GS view of -5% US CER growth. The Medicare IRA price decision is expected by November 30 2026.

Neuro-muscular setbacks: del-desiran failed in Phase III, and Novartis is reassessing trial design ahead of FDA talks on a second Phase III. For Zolgensma, management acknowledged an emerging AAV tumorigenicity risk after two cases of vector integration near an oncogene.

Novartis sees ianalumab as potentially category-creating in Sjögren's disease. The key near-term risk is label scope, as FDA discussions focus on responder subsets. Launch is expected to be a steady build.

Cardiovascular: the HORIZON Lp(a) trial failed, and GS sees limited probability of success in a similar population. Novartis points to DII235 lowering Lp(a) by up to 95% vs. 78% in HORIZON and to higher discontinuations in the pelacarsen arm.

Novartis presented AI in drug development as a long-term driver, citing a data lake built since 2017. GS expects benefits to take time, with patient selection and recruitment speed likely to show earlier.
Valuation: the GS 12-month price target is CHF 113 / $136 per ADR, a 50:50 blend of DCF (CHF 110) and 13.5x 2027/28E P/E (CHF 117). This implies downside of 11.2% for NOVN.S and 10.1% for NVS.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Sell with a $136 ADR target (CHF 113 for NOVN.S), citing patent expirations at the end of the decade and a challenging MSD growth ambition beyond 2030 without more late-stage M&A or clinical success.

earnings_insights: GS forecasts (estimates, not reported): 2026E EPS $9.01 (basic pre-exceptionals $9.09), 2027E EPS $10.08, 2028E EPS $10.69. 2025 reported EPS was $8.91 (basic pre-exceptionals $8.98).
GS forecasts revenue of $56.5bn in 2026E, $60.3bn in 2027E and $62.6bn in 2028E. 2025 revenue was $54.5bn.
Strong FCF reported by the company: $17.6bn in 2025 and $14bn through 9M26.
GS forecasts Q4 2026E EPS of $2.19, Q1 2027E $2.21 and Q2 2027E $2.57 (estimates). The Q3 2026 figure shown is $2.45.
risk_factors: Patent expirations for Entresto, Cosentyx, Kesimpta and Kisqali could push growth below 5% CAGR in 2031/32.
Clinical trial execution risk on pipeline assets, including recent failures (del-desiran Phase III, pelacarsen in HORIZON, pacibekitug read-through from ZEUS).
Emerging AAV tumorigenicity risk for Zolgensma.
Label scope risk for ianalumab in Sjögren's disease.

Upside risks to the GS Sell view: ongoing positive earnings momentum, stronger-than-anticipated sales from key franchises, unexpected pipeline success, and capital allocation priorities including BD and buybacks.
geopolitical: IRA (US Inflation Reduction Act) Medicare pricing: Cosentyx pricing takes effect in 2028 and Kisqali is under pressure in 2028, with the Medicare decision for Kisqali expected by November 30 2026.

tension_points.bull_case: Management reiterates mid-single-digit growth beyond 2030, with a $20bn gap to 2035 consensus. It says near-term assets (remibrutinib, ianalumab, pelabresib, Actinium-PSMA, abelacimab) could close the first c.$10bn, and 35 submission-enabling readouts run through 2031. The 2026-31 5% CAGR guide implies about 3% upside to consensus 2031 sales.
tension_points.bear_case: GS says the cadence of patent expirations for Entresto, Cosentyx, Kesimpta and Kisqali could produce growth below 5% into 2031/32. GS excludes Phase 1 assets from forecasts, and the roughly 15x 2028 P/E already partly reflects the growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Additional late-stage M&A or above-average clinical trial success and indication de-risking, which GS says would be needed for the MSD ambition to look achievable.

theme_stances.key_argument: MSD growth beyond 2030 looks challenging absent more late-stage M&A or above-average clinical success, so GS stays Sell.
theme_stances.evidence: continues to look challenging in the absence of any additional late-stage M&A
